name: DHT11 temperature & humidity module (KY-015)
description: Aosong DHT11 basic temperature (0 to 50 °C, ±2 °C) and relative humidity (20–90 %RH, ±5 %RH) sensor with a single-wire digital output, 1 °C / 1 %RH resolution, read at most every 1–2 s. Runs on 3.3–5.5 V. Sold as: KY-015 DHT11 temperature & humidity module (37-in-1 sensor kit board, 3-pin header S, +, - with the DATA pull-up resistor fitted on the board).
eli5: A little blue box that tells your board roughly how warm the room is and how damp the air is, over one wire.

pins.name: S
pins.description: DATA: single-wire bidirectional data line (pull-up fitted on the module)

supplierQuery: KY-015 DHT11 temperature humidity sensor module
buildNotes: Wire S to a GPIO that can output as well as input (not GPIO 34-39 on an ESP32), + to 3V3 (or 5 V) and - to GND. The module already has the pull-up on S, so no extra resistor is needed.

Use MicroPython's built-in dht module: dht.DHT11(Pin(n)), then measure() and temperature()/humidity(). It sends the 18 ms start pulse, reads the 40 bits and checks the checksum for you; a bad checksum or no answer raises OSError.
Read no more often than about every 2 s; each reading returns the result of the previous measurement, so after a long pause the first value can be stale.
On 3.3 V keep the wires short (under 1 m, per the datasheet). Wait about 1 s after power-up before the first reading.
Readings are whole numbers only (1 °C, 1 %RH steps) and only valid from 0 to 50 °C and 20 to 90 %RH. For better accuracy use a DHT22/AM2302.
Some KY-015 clones print the pins in a different order (e.g. - in the middle): always follow the labels printed on your board.

test.title: Reports the temperature and humidity set on the sliders

library.note: Passed the Sparkbench part check in simulation and matched an independent datasheet reading (2 difference(s) settled by a third reading with quoted evidence). Not yet tested on real hardware.
